Bash(git commit -m "$\(cat <<''EOF''
Fix triage_database import errors in thumbnail modules

Fixed "No module named 'triage_database'" errors that were appearing in logs
when the thumbnail cache attempted to update metadata.

Problem:
- thumbnail_generator.py and thumbnail_cache.py used relative imports
- from triage_database import TriageDatabase
- When called from main app, module not found

Solution:
- Changed all imports to absolute: from triage.triage_database import TriageDatabase
- Consistent with thumbnail_cache.py top-level imports
- Works correctly when imported from main application

Files Modified:
- triage/thumbnail_generator.py: 2 import statements fixed
- triage/thumbnail_cache.py: 1 import statement fixed

This eliminates the "Failed to update thumbnail cache metadata" errors in logs.

Bash(git commit -m "$\(cat <<''EOF''
Add file action buttons to preview window

Added three file operation buttons to the bottom of the detachable preview window
for quick access to source file operations.

New Buttons:
- Open File: Opens source file with default application
- Open Folder: Opens folder containing source file \(with file selected on Windows/macOS\)
- Copy Path: Copies source file path to clipboard

Features:
- Platform-independent implementation \(Windows/macOS/Linux\)
- Buttons auto-enable/disable based on whether source file exists
- Spacer pushes "Correct Date" and "Close" buttons to the right
- Clear error logging for troubleshooting

Implementation Details:
- Windows: Uses os.startfile\(\) for files, explorer /select for folders
- macOS: Uses ''open'' command for files, ''open -R'' to reveal in Finder
- Linux: Uses xdg-open for both files and folders
- Clipboard: Uses QApplication.clipboard\(\) for cross-platform copy

Benefits:
- Quick access to original source files
- Easy navigation to file location
- Convenient path copying for documentation/troubleshooting

Bash(git commit -m "$\(cat <<''EOF''
Make thumbnail cache size configurable with 500MB default

Added user-configurable thumbnail cache memory size and worker thread settings.

Database Schema Changes:
- Added cache_memory_mb column \(INTEGER DEFAULT 500\)
- Added cache_worker_threads column \(INTEGER DEFAULT 8\)
- Automatic upgrade for old databases

New DatabaseMetadata Methods \(database_metadata.py\):
- get_cache_memory_mb\(\) - Returns cache memory size in MB \(default: 500MB\)
- set_cache_memory_mb\(size_mb\) - Set cache memory size
- get_cache_worker_threads\(\) - Returns worker thread count \(default: 8\)
- set_cache_worker_threads\(threads\) - Set worker thread count

Date Corrections Tab \(ui/date_corrections_tab.py\):
- Reads cache settings from database instead of hardcoded values
- Calculates memory_items from MB setting \(~150KB per thumbnail\)
- Logs cache configuration on initialization
- Default 500MB = ~3,413 thumbnails \(vs previous 500 items = ~75MB\)

Settings Tab UI \(ui/settings_tab.py\):
- New "Thumbnail Cache Settings" group in General tab
- Cache memory size spinner \(50-2000 MB range\)
- Worker threads spinner \(1-16 threads range\)
- Real-time item count display \(~X,XXX thumbnails\)
- CPU core count hint for optimal thread setting
- Help text explaining impact of settings
- Auto-saves to database on value change
- Loads from database when database selected

Benefits:
- 500MB default = ~6.8x more thumbnails cached \(3,413 vs 500\)
- Users can tune based on their system RAM
- Low-memory systems: Reduce to 100-250MB
- High-memory systems: Increase to 1000-2000MB
- Worker threads match CPU cores for optimal generation speed
- Settings persist per database

Example Configurations:
- 100MB = ~683 thumbnails \(~3GB RAM systems\)
- 500MB = ~3,413 thumbnails \(~8GB RAM systems\) [DEFAULT]
- 1000MB = ~6,826 thumbnails \(~16GB RAM systems\)
- 2000MB = ~13,653 thumbnails \(~32GB RAM systems\)
